item.title: Nebuta Museum WA RASSE: Aomori's Festival Year-Round — Guide
item.description: Right beside Aomori Station, the Nebuta Museum WA RASSE lets you experience Aomori’s greatest festival any day of the year. Five of the towering illuminated warrior floats from recent Nebuta Festivals are displayed indoors, close enough to see every brushstroke and wire. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Aomori City (by Aomori Station) Hours 9:00–18:00 (seasonal) Admission Around ¥620 Time needed About 1–1.

item.title: Nara National Museum: Buddhist Art & Shosoin — Guide
item.description: The Nara National Museum, on the edge of Nara Park, holds one of Japan’s finest collections of Buddhist sculpture and art. Its elegant Meiji-era Nara Hall and modern galleries are best known for the prestigious annual Shosoin Exhibition each autumn, showing imperial treasures from Todai-ji’s 8th-century repository. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Noborioji-cho, Nara Park Hours 9:30–17:00, closed Mondays Admission ¥700 permanent (special exhibitions higher) Time needed 1–1.

item.title: Upopoy Ainu Museum Guide: Tickets, Highlights & Access
item.description: Upopoy (the National Ainu Museum and Park) at Shiraoi is Japan’s flagship centre for the culture of the Ainu, the Indigenous people of Hokkaido and the north. Opened in 2020 on the shore of Lake Poroto, this thoughtful complex tells the Ainu story — their language, beliefs, crafts and connection to nature — long marginalised and now celebrated. With a modern museum, traditional houses, live music and dance, craft demonstrations and hands-on workshops, Upopoy is a moving, eye-opening stop that adds real depth to a Hokkaido trip.

item.title: Kurashiki Bikan Quarter: Canal District, Ohara Museum, and Craft Shopping
item.description: Kurashiki sits 16 minutes west of Okayama by train, but in character it belongs to a different world. Where Okayama City is a modern prefectural capital with castle gardens and department stores, Kurashiki preserves a dense quarter of Edo-period architecture that survived the 20th century largely intact. The Bikan Historic Quarter — a cluster of white-walled earthen storehouses (kura) along a narrow canal lined with willows — is among the best-preserved merchant districts in Japan, and one of the few that has found a productive second life as a center for arts and crafts rather than simply as a museum piece.
